name: power-or-pmos
title: Two supplies ORed: USB through a Schottky, the other one through back-to-back P-MOSFETs
about: Two supplies onto one rail, neither one fed backwards (hint HINT.two_supplies). The preferred supply (usb) reaches the rail through an SS34; the other one (bat: cells or a second input) through two AO3401A in series with a common source, whose gates usb pulls up. While usb is present both MOSFETs are off and their body diodes point against each other: bat is cut off in both directions. Without usb, R1 pulls the gates to ground and bat feeds the rail with milliohms instead of a diode drop. As built in the reference project (pytree D-44, Q8/Q9, D40).

ports.bat: the supply that is cut off while usb is present: cells or a second input
ports.usb: the preferred supply, e.g. USB VBUS behind its fuse; it drives the gates

components.label: {as}: bat cut-off PMOS, drain at bat
{as}: bat cut-off PMOS, drain at the rail

nets.name: mid
nets.notes: Common source of the back-to-back pair.

notes: Both MOSFETs stay off only while bat stays below usb + |VGS(th)|. Above it they conduct in part: fresh lithium AA cells (5.4 V) against USB at 4.75 V with the worst-case VGS(th) of -0.5 V gave about 0.18 A and 0.17 W in the reference project (M-1). The simulation uses the typical threshold.
AO3401A: VGS max ±12 V – both supplies up to about 10 V, as for reverse-pmos; 3.2 A at 70 °C, 85 mΩ at VGS -2.5 V.
A reversed bat meets Q1's drain with source and gate outside (PATH.reverse): give the connector or holder of bat "source": "reversible". The block replaces reverse-pmos on that input.
sim.json: both supplies as sources, scenarios with each one alone and with both at mismatched voltages (bat high, usb low and the other way round); in none of them may a source take current.

While usb ramps up or down (1–20 ms) neither path may conduct for a moment – the MOSFETs are half off, D1 does not conduct yet. A large load can brown out; the reference project accepted a restart under full load.
A Schottky in the bat path instead would cost 0.3–0.4 V, often the whole reserve of a battery.
